title: Our process — Supreme Art
description: Follow every carton through Pre press, Press and Offpress at Supreme Art, from artwork and plate preparation to finishing and delivery.
intro: Scroll through every stage — from the initial design to the packed cartons delivered to your facility, each production step is carefully controlled under one roof in Peshawar.

steps.title: Designing
steps.text: Artwork and carton layouts are created and prepared by our in-house design team.

steps.title: Plate making
steps.text: Using our computer-to-plate (CTP) system, printing plates are produced for the offset press.

steps.title: Cutting
steps.text: Stock paperboard is cut to the precise sheet size required by the printing machine.

steps.title: Printing
steps.text: The approved carton design is printed onto the prepared sheets using offset printing presses.

steps.title: Proofing & QC
steps.text: Our quality-control team checks colour shades, registration and text content against the approved proof.

steps.title: Coating
steps.text: The printed sheets receive the specified protective or decorative coating for the required finish.

steps.title: Die-cutting
steps.text: The coated sheets are cut and creased into individual unit-carton blanks.

steps.title: Breaking
steps.text: Waste board is removed from around the die-cut cartons, separating the individual blanks cleanly.

steps.title: Sorting
steps.text: An automated inspection machine uses 3D cameras to check every unit carton for colour, print and overall quality.

steps.title: Pasting & folder gluing
steps.text: The inspected unit cartons are folded, glued and joined before being packed into bundles or boxes.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.text: The finished cartons are securely packed and delivered to the client, ready for the filling line.

cta.heading: Have a carton to make?
cta.text: Send us your artwork or dieline — we'll come back with a quote and a timeline.

scenes.lead: From the first idea to the approved artwork.
scenes.detail: Our designers prepare the carton layout, arranging its panels, text and colours on screen. Printed artwork is then reviewed alongside the samples, so every detail is checked before plate preparation.

photos.caption: Preparing the carton layout
photos.alt: Designer preparing carton artwork on a computer.

photos.caption: Refining the artwork
photos.alt: Designer working on packaging artwork at an iMac.

photos.caption: Checking the printed layout
photos.alt: Printed carton layouts being reviewed on a worktable.

scenes.detail: The approved artwork is transferred to a blue-coated aluminium plate on our computer-to-plate (CTP) system. The plate then passes through the processor, which cleans away the coating and reveals the image areas.

photos.caption: CTP plate preparation
photos.alt: Blue printing plate loaded into CTP equipment.

photos.caption: Processing and cleaning
photos.alt: Printing plate passing through processor rollers.

scenes.detail: Each processed plate is checked for a clear, complete image, then kept in labelled storage so the right plate is ready for the right job.

photos.caption: The prepared plate
photos.alt: Processed printing plate with visible image areas.

photos.caption: Organised plate storage
photos.alt: Printing plates stored in labelled glass-fronted cabinets.

scenes.lead: The right sheets, ready for the press.
scenes.detail: Paperboard is kept in wrapped stacks, then moved to the cutting area on a pallet lifter. The operator aligns the stack at the guillotine and cuts it to the sheet size the job needs. Plates and paperboard are now ready for Press.

photos.caption: Paperboard stock
photos.alt: Wrapped paperboard on pallets.

photos.caption: Moving the material
photos.alt: A pallet lifter carrying paperboard to production.

photos.caption: Cutting to sheet size
photos.alt: Operator aligning paperboard at a guillotine cutter.

scenes.detail: Before the run, each printing unit is charged with the process and spot colours the job needs. The sheet then travels through the units in sequence, taking on one ink after another.

photos.caption: Charging the ink units
photos.alt: Press operator loading ink tins on top of the printing units.

photos.caption: A multi-colour press line
photos.alt: Multi-colour offset press line with a stack of paperboard at the feeder.

scenes.detail: With the cut sheets loaded at the feeder, the run starts. Our Heidelberg Speedmaster CD 102 and SM-74 presses print multi-colour work with consistent registration from sheet to sheet.

photos.caption: Starting the run
photos.alt: Operator starting the press beside printed sheets on the delivery table.

photos.caption: Heidelberg Speedmaster CD 102
photos.alt: Heidelberg Speedmaster CD 102 multi-colour printing press.

photos.caption: Offset Machine 3, Heidelberg SM-74
photos.alt: Operator at the controls of Offset Machine 3, a Heidelberg SM-74.

scenes.detail: A handheld spectrophotometer reads the printed sheet against the approved colour targets. At the console, the sheet is compared with the approved proof and the ink zones are adjusted until every carton matches.

photos.caption: Measuring colour
photos.alt: Operator measuring a printed sheet with a handheld spectrophotometer.

photos.caption: Matching the approved proof
photos.alt: Operator comparing a printed sheet with the approved proof at the press console.

photos.caption: On press
photos.alt: Offset printing press.

scenes.lead: A finish that protects and shines.
scenes.detail: Printed sheets travel flat through the coating line, where a gloss finish deepens the colours and protects the artwork. Spot finishes add raised, textured detail to selected areas.

photos.caption: Through the coating line
photos.alt: Printed sheets running flat through the coating line under guide wheels.

photos.caption: A gloss-coated sheet
photos.alt: Gloss-coated sheet of orange Movonac-D cartons with its colour bar.

photos.caption: Spot finish detail
photos.alt: IV SIP carton sheet with a raised, textured spot finish on selected areas.

scenes.lead: Checked from the first sheet to the last.
scenes.detail: Finished sheets are measured with handheld instruments and checked against the targets approved for the job before they move on to cutting.

photos.caption: Checking the finish
photos.alt: Operator checking a coated sheet.

photos.caption: Measuring the sheet
photos.alt: Operator measuring a finished sheet beside Offset Machine 8.

photos.caption: Checking the stack
photos.alt: Operator checking the top sheet of a finished stack.

scenes.detail: Every carton design has its own cutting die, kept in labelled racks. Our automatic die-cutters, including a YH-1060 and an SP 102-E, cut and crease full sheets at production speed.

photos.caption: Cutting dies in storage
photos.alt: Rows of Supreme Art cutting dies stored upright in racks.

photos.caption: Automatic die-cutters
photos.alt: Automatic die-cutters, a YH-1060 and an SP 102-E, on the factory floor.

photos.caption: Setting up the die-cutter
photos.alt: Operator at the controls of the SP 102-E die-cutter.

scenes.detail: Some jobs run on a platen die-cutter. Waste board is then removed from around the cut cartons, and every unit carton is inspected before it moves on to folding.

photos.caption: Platen die-cutting
photos.alt: Two operators lifting a cut sheet from a platen die-cutter as punched pieces fall clear.

photos.caption: Removing waste board
photos.alt: Operator removing waste board from a stack of die-cut sheets.

photos.caption: Inspecting unit cartons
photos.alt: Operator inspecting unit cartons by hand.

scenes.detail: On our folder-gluers, including a Bobst Expert 105 A, the carton blanks are folded, glued and joined in one continuous run.

photos.caption: Folder gluing
photos.alt: Operators running cartons through a folder-gluer.

photos.caption: Bobst Expert 105 A
photos.alt: Bobst Expert 105 A folder-gluer running printed cartons.

scenes.detail: Finished cartons are packed into labelled shipping boxes, held in store and loaded for delivery to the client, ready for the filling line.

photos.caption: Ready for dispatch
photos.alt: Rows of labelled, sealed shipping boxes in the finished-goods store.

photos.caption: Palletised for delivery
photos.alt: Packed cartons stacked on a pallet at the loading bay.

photos.caption: Loading for delivery
photos.alt: Worker loading labelled boxes into a shipping container.
